A couplet is defined as "two lines of poetry that have identical or similar rhyme schemes." The first line ends with the final word from the previous line; this can be repeated on the second line if desired. A rhyming pattern consists of two lines which end in words having matching sounds (called "rhymes").

author: william_wordsworth
text:
O bright fair star, o splendour of the west !
 Thy drooping head shall never bow or sink ;
 Till, after some time more than now we jest,
 Some cloud may hide thee from our view at night :

Till then, like thy sister-stars thou dost shine,
 And cheer us all; for where’er thou art seen,
 No clouds can cover thee but thine own line,
 Or that which runs about thy crown between.
